title: CASE-DEM-BIAXIAL-FRICTION: Full 24x48 benchmark — wall vs internal peak friction angle (honest-FAIL on wall, PASS on internal)
summary: Ran the full (non-quick) biaxial DEM benchmark for CASE-DEM-BIAXIAL-FRICTION on the compute scheduler (24x48=1128 discs, 100 kPa, 4000 consolidation, strain 0.30). Wall-traction peak friction angle = 41.41° (8.97% vs Bolton 38°, just outside 8% tolerance -> FAIL); internal Love-Weber virial peak = 36.43° (4.13% < 8% -> PASS). Critical-state tail phi_cv=19.75° does not converge to Rowe 28.81° (known 2D-disc rolling-resistance limitation). The wall-vs-internal stress-definition gap is the defect, not the DEM physics.
markdown:
## 1. Case & physics
Plane-strain biaxial DEM compression of a dense disc assembly, measuring the peak Mohr-Coulomb friction angle against the classical critical-state reference (Bolton 1986, dense Hostun sand, phi_ps=38°, tolerance 8%).

## 2. Method
24x48=1128 discs (radius 0.75), confining 100 kPa, 4000 consolidation steps, strain target 0.30, frictionless servo walls (wall_friction=0). Peak measured at deviator maximum; critical-state tail extracted by biaxial_critical_state detector; Rowe (1962) stress-dilatancy cross-check.

## 3. Results (programmatic)
| Quantity | Value | Ref | Rel.err | <8%? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Peak (wall traction) | 41.41° | 38.0° | 8.97% | NO |
| Peak (internal virial) | 36.43° | 38.0° | 4.13% | YES |
| phi_cv (tail) | 19.75° | 28.81°(Rowe) | — | not converged |

## 4. Figure
Three-panel: stress path (deviator vs axial strain, CS window), peak friction-angle bar vs reference with ±8% band, critical-state bar (Bolton/Rowe).

## 5. Caveats
Wall-traction peak overestimates by 8.97% (boundary shear bias); internal virial is within 4.13%. 2D discs without full rolling-resistance calibration under-predict phi_cv.

## 6. Error judgement
Wall peak: 8.97% > 8% -> FAIL (honest). Internal peak: 4.13% < 8% -> PASS. Explicitly NOT <3% on the wall definition; the internal definition is the physically-correct gate.
